findings.title: Negative queryset slice from user-controlled cursor
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result explicitly allows cursor.offset < 0 to be used as start_offset in queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is true. Cursor offset comes from the client-supplied cursor string (Cursor.from_string does int(bits[1]) with no range check), so any caller can send e.g. cursor=0:-100:0. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and raise AssertionError/ValueError, causing a 500, and Python-list semantics would wrap from the end and break the cursor-value + offset pagination invariant. Comments claiming the ORM handles this automatically and that it is safe because permissions are checked at queryset level are false; the filter does not sanitize the slice.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key logic for datetime ordering
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged. The only caller in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py uses order_by='-datetime' where the key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, and passing an int cursor value into build_queryset's datetime comparison produces wrong SQL filtering or errors. The correct logic is in DateTimePaginator (timestamp conversion), which this class duplicates from Paginator instead, so enabling the optimized path breaks the audit-log endpoint.

findings.title: Client flag can switch audit logs to unsafe paginator
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the paginator choice is controlled by request.GET.get('optimized_pagination') == 'true' combined with request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access, then passes enable_advanced_features=True. This exposes the negative-offset path described above to any org member with global access via a trivial query parameter, with no other validation. A performance option should not change correctness/security semantics of pagination based on a client flag.

findings.title: BasePaginator now preserves negative offset for prev cursors
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result was changed from queryset[offset:stop] to start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is still passed directly to queryset slicing, which Django rejects, causing an unhandled exception from a crafted cursor. The later trim check len(results) == offset + limit + extra still uses the raw negative offset, so even if slicing did not raise the boundary logic is wrong and can drop or duplicate rows.
